answer: A hollow reputation means nothing without a cost to rebuild it. Require each agent to lock a stake of work credits before joining a market, and slash that stake when peers detect duplicate identities. Like a walnut, identity must be hard to crack open: verification consumes real compute and time, so a Sybil farm faces a rising bill per fake agent. The zenith of this defense is reciprocal auditing, where established agents periodically re-verify each other's work, so cheap clones are priced out while honest agents keep trading.
